scope: Final GPU serving only. Original training, candidate grids, validation/calibration choices, quality budgets and held-out audits stay fixed under memory_application_frontier_v1.json.
real_batches: Batch 1 uses original official test prefixes. Batch 8 uses eight distinct official prefixes of exactly equal token length; take the earliest complete groups in official case/group traversal order, without padding or position changes. Record all case IDs, groups, input hash and total unique prompt count.
device_isolation: All quality, construction and training stages must finish first. Each GPU executes one fresh worker at a time. Assign one model/seed to a fixed GPU, including its source, independent controls, matched raw/native controls and frozen selected codecs. Different physical GPUs may run concurrently; CPU final query timers run after the GPU queue, serially.
host_affinity: Preassign disjoint allowed CPU sets near each GPU where topology permits; record actual worker affinity, topology and host load. Parallel device runs share the host memory subsystem, so only selected-GPU isolation is claimed.
competition: NVML must show no external compute clients before loading, during every request and after measurement. Preserve unknown training/evaluation processes and fail or wait if they compete. User-confirmed occupancy cleanup is outside benchmark code.
correctness_preflight: Both model families must pass source/native cached logit and generation byte comparisons on actual batch 1 and distinct-request batch 8 before the final timing queues.
reason: Use all available hardware while retaining per-device matched comparisons, and replace repeated-prompt batching with actual heterogeneous official inputs. This amendment precedes any accepted final timing result and does not use test outcomes to choose a codec.
